How the compliance app works

For the facilities team. Tap the menu at the top to jump to any part.

What the app isThe three parts, and how a month works

This is the Big Sky compliance app. It runs in the browser on your phone, and you use it once a month to check emergency lighting, fire extinguishers, fire doors and water temperatures in every space.

There are three parts, and they work together:

  • The Checklist (this app, on your phone). You go space by space and tap Pass or Fail.
  • The Maintenance List (a shared Google Sheet, shown in the app). Anything that fails is put on it automatically, so nothing gets forgotten.
  • The monthly email to facilities@bigskylondon.com. The app writes it for you. You paste it into an email and attach the PDFs.

The month at a glance

1. Check each space on your phone. Pass or Fail every item.
↓
2. Generate PDFs for the space. Save them to Drive.
↓
3. The Maintenance List updates by itself in the background.
↓
4. Chase the open items and mark them resolved when fixed.
↓
5. Send the monthly email with the PDFs attached.
Never lose work. Everything you tick or type is saved on your phone as you go, so you can stop halfway and come back. If you have no signal, the app keeps what it could not send and tries again by itself.
The ? dots and the Help? button inside the app explain each part on the screen where you are. This guide is the long version.
Open the compliance app
The monthly routineEight steps, in order

Do this for every space, once a month.

  1. Open the app and type your name in the box at the top. It is printed on the PDFs as “Checked by”.
  2. Pick the building and the space from the two drop-downs.
  3. Open each section (Emergency Lighting, Fire Extinguishers, Fire Doors, Water Temperature) and tap Pass or Fail on every item. For water, type the hot and cold readings first.
  4. If something fails, say what is wrong in the red box. Say what you did about it in Action taken, or tick Fixed on the spot if you sorted it there and then.
  5. Tap “Generate PDFs for this space” at the bottom, pick the sections you did, and save the PDFs to Drive when your phone’s share sheet opens.
  6. Repeat for the next space. If a section cannot be done (for example the water is off), generate the PDFs for the ones you did. The space shows 3/4 this month and the missing section is marked To do until you come back to it.
  7. Go to the Maintenance List tab to see what is open. Add an Action note to anything you are chasing, and tap Mark resolved once it is properly fixed.
  8. At the end of the month, tap Monthly summary email, paste it into an email to facilities, attach the PDFs and send.
Doing the checksPass, Fail, notes, actions, water and progress

The top of the screen

  • Your name. Printed on every PDF as “Checked by”. Type it once; the app remembers it.
  • Building and space. Pick where you are. Everything below is for that space only.
  • Status. All clear or Needs attention. Attention means something is marked Fail here, or is still open on the Maintenance List. Next to it is how far through the month the space is (see Progress this month below).
  • A section. Tap to open or close. A red dot means something inside is flagged.
  • Generate PDFs for this space. Always at the bottom of the screen.
  • Help? Opens a short explanation of the screen you are on. It never opens by itself.

Progress this month

Some months a section cannot be finished, for example when contractors have the water off. The app shows exactly what is left, so the space does not look unchecked.

  • 3/4 this month. Three of the four sections have had PDFs generated this month. When all four are done it changes to ✓ Done for Nov.
  • To do. Marks the section that is still outstanding. It only appears once at least one section is done, so it never nags at the start of a month.

To finish the month, do the missing section later and generate its PDF. The tag then changes to Done, and the To do marker goes away. At the start of a new month it resets by itself.

Pass and Fail

Every item starts on Pass, so you only need to touch the ones that are not right. This works the same way for lights, extinguishers, fire doors and water outlets.

  • Pass / Fail. Tap Fail if there is a problem. Tap Pass again to undo it; the failure text is cleared.
  • What’s wrong. Say it plainly, e.g. “Light not coming on”. This is the wording that goes on the Maintenance List and in the email. If the item is already open on the list, its existing wording is filled in for you.
  • Action taken. What is being done about it, e.g. “Electrician booked for Friday”. It is printed on the PDF and copied to the Action note on the Maintenance List.
  • Fixed on the spot. Tick it if you sorted the problem there and then. The fail and what you did stay on the PDF, but it is not put on the Maintenance List and is left out of the monthly email. If it was already on the list, it is marked resolved.
  • Mark all pass. Resets every item in that section to Pass in one tap. Handy when everything is fine.
Always explain a Fail. If you tap Fail and leave the box empty, the Maintenance List says “Marked Fail (no note added)”, which does not help whoever has to fix it.

Water temperature

Most outlets are fine, so leave them on Pass and just type the readings. If one is wrong, for example the hot tap only reaches 46°C, tap Fail. You can usually put it right yourself, so tick Fixed on the spot and say what you did. That way the PDF shows the problem and how it was dealt with, without cluttering the Maintenance List.

  • Pass / Fail. Same as every other check.
  • Hot reading in °C.
  • Cold reading in °C.
  • Water flushed through. Ticked for you; untick it if you did not flush.
  • What’s wrong. Appears when you tap Fail.
  • Action taken. E.g. “Ran the taps for 3 minutes”.
  • Fixed on the spot. Tick it if it is sorted.
The app does not flag a low reading by itself. You decide: Pass if it is fine, Fail if it is not.
Making the PDFsAnd what happens afterwards

Generate the PDFs once you have finished a space. This is also what tells the Maintenance List the space has been checked.

  • Sections to include. Only tick the ones you actually went through. Sections with no checkpoints are not offered.
  • Generate. Makes one PDF per ticked section.
  1. Tap Generate PDFs for this space.
  2. Tick the sections you did, then tap Generate.
  3. On a phone, the share sheet opens. Save the PDFs to Drive (or Files). On a computer they download.

What happens in the background

  • The Maintenance List is updated to match your checklist. New fails are added; ones already on the list get the latest wording and Action note; anything marked Fixed on the spot is resolved.
  • The date checked is recorded for each section you generated, which resets the Due tags.
  • This happens even if you close the share sheet without saving.
  • If you have no signal, the app saves the update and sends it when you are back online. A line under the title says an update is waiting until it has gone.
Re-generating is safe. Run it again after changing a note and the list is overwritten with what the checklist now says. It never creates duplicates.
If something is Fail on the checklist but was resolved on the list, the app puts it back on the list as open, because the checklist says it is still a problem. Tap Pass first if it really is fixed.
The Maintenance ListChasing and resolving issues

The shared list of everything that needs attention, grouped by space. Anyone with the app sees the same list.

  • Refresh. Reloads the list. It also refreshes by itself every minute.
  • Monthly summary email. See the next section.
  • A space. Tap to open and see its issues. 2 open or Clear shows how many it has.
  • Progress and due tags. ✓ Done for Nov or 3/4 this month, then the Due tags if the space is overdue.

Open Sheet (next to Refresh) opens a short popup that explains the Google Sheet the list is stored in, with a button to open it if you want to see everything in one table. You never need it for day-to-day use.

Progress on the list

Each space shows the same progress tag as the checklist. Open the space and a yellow line tells you which section is still to do.

  • 3/4 this month. The same tag as on the checklist.
  • Still to do this month. Names the section that has not been done yet.

Working through an issue

  • The issue as written when it was flagged, and the date.
  • Action note. Type what is happening, e.g. “Engineer booked 3 Dec”. It is saved as you type and shows in the monthly email.
  • Mark resolved. Tap when it is properly fixed. It leaves the open list and is not in next month’s email.

The coloured tags

All clear Needs attentionTop of a space on the Checklist.
3/4 this month ✓ Done for NovHow many sections have had PDFs generated this month. 3/4 means one is still to do. Done means all of them are.
Last checked 12 NovShown at the start of a month, before any section is done: the date PDFs were last generated, using the oldest across its sections. “Not yet checked” means a section has never been through a PDF run.
Due soon Due UrgentMaintenance List only. Due soon at 3 weeks since the last check, Due at 1 month, Urgent at 2 months, counted from the oldest section. Generating the PDFs resets it.
⚠ Open on Maintenance ListShown under an item on the Checklist that is already on the list, with the reason.
The monthly summary emailCopy, paste, attach, send

At the end of the month the app writes the email for you. It says which spaces were fully checked and lists only what is still outstanding. Anything marked resolved or fixed on the spot is left out.

  • Month. Defaults to this month. Pick an earlier one to look back.
  • Preview. Read it before sending. A yellow box at the top lists spaces not fully checked yet.
  • Copy email body. Copies it as formatted text.
  • Copy body and open my email app. The quickest way: it starts a new email to facilities@bigskylondon.com with the subject filled in and copies the body.
  1. Tap Monthly summary email on the Maintenance List tab.
  2. Tap Copy body and open my email app.
  3. Paste into the new email (long-press on a phone, Ctrl+V or Cmd+V on a computer). Pasting keeps your email signature.
  4. Attach the PDFs from Drive, then send.
Satellite sites (Omega Place, 14A, Hoxton) are not included in this email. Each satellite manager sends their own, from their own page.
Satellite sitesLinks and guides for site managers

Each satellite site has its own page that shows only that site. The manager does their checks there, and anything they fail goes onto the same Maintenance List under Satellite sites.

  • Open page. Shows the site’s page, so you can see what the manager sees.
  • Copy link. Copies the address to send to the manager.

The site pages and guides

Omega PlaceOpen pageGuide
14AOpen pageGuide
HoxtonOpen pageGuide

Setting a manager up

  1. Tap Copy link for their site and send it to them. Send each manager only their own link.
  2. Send them their short guide too. It is a one-page instruction written just for them. It also opens from the Full guide button inside their app’s Help.
  3. Ask them to add their page to their phone’s Home Screen so it opens like an app. The guide shows how.
What managers do each month: type their name, Pass or Fail each item, tap Generate PDFs, then tap Monthly email to facilities, paste it into an email and attach the PDFs. That is all.

Sites with sections showing “No checkpoints added yet” (14A and Hoxton, for now) are fine: the manager skips those. Add their checkpoints with Edit checkpoints when you know them (see below).

Editing checkpointsAdd, rename, remove, make permanent

Tap Edit checkpoints under the space picker to change what is checked in a space. While it is on, results are not recorded.

  • Pencil. Rename the checkpoint.
  • ✕. Remove it.
  • Drag handle (⋮⋮). Press and hold a row, or grab the handle, then drag it into a new order.

To add one, tap the + at the bottom of the section, type the name (for extinguishers, pick the type), and save.

Changes only live on that phone until they are made permanent. If you rename or add a checkpoint and someone else opens the app, they will not see it.

Making changes permanent for everyone

  1. Turn on Edit checkpoints and tap Export All at the bottom.
  2. Copy the text it gives you.
  3. Send it to whoever looks after the app. They build it into the next version, and everyone gets it when the app is updated.

Reset “Studio 1” data (the small link at the bottom of a space) clears that space’s ticks and notes on this phone only, in case you want to start it again. It does not touch the Maintenance List.

Something went wrongQuestions and answers
I tapped Fail by mistake.
Tap Pass. The note and action are cleared. If you already generated PDFs, the Maintenance List entry is fixed the next time you generate.
An item on the Maintenance List is wrong or out of date.
Change the wording on the Checklist (Fail, edit the box) and generate the PDFs again. The list is overwritten to match. Or just type an Action note on the list itself.
It says an update is waiting.
There was no signal when you generated. The app keeps the update and sends it by itself, usually within a minute of being back online. Keep the app open for a moment.
The app says to update the Maintenance List script.
The Google script is out of date. See Admin, “Update the Google script”. Your items are still sent the older way meanwhile.
The Maintenance List is empty or will not load.
Tap Refresh. If it still fails, check the phone has signal, then try again in a minute.
A space says “3/4 this month” but I could not do the last section.
That is correct. Generate the PDFs for the sections you did. The one still to do is marked To do, and the Maintenance List names it. Come back, finish it, generate its PDF, and the space changes to Done.
A space says “Not yet checked”.
At least one of its sections has never been through a PDF run. Generate PDFs for each section you have done.
The Help box keeps popping up.
It no longer opens by itself. Tap Help? at the top right whenever you want it.
A section says “No checkpoints added yet”.
Nothing is set up there. Skip it, or add checkpoints with Edit checkpoints.
I typed in a box and the screen jumped.
This is fixed. The page no longer refreshes under you, and the box grows so you can always see what you type. If it ever happens again, tell facilities which phone and browser.
My checklist is different to a colleague’s.
Checkpoint edits are per phone until made permanent. Export All and send it on.
The app looks old or is missing something I was told about.
Check the version at the top right. Close the tab and reopen it; on iPhone, pull down to refresh. If it is still old, the update has not been uploaded yet.
How the app is set upThe pieces, and how they fit together

A plain description of how the whole system fits together, for whoever looks after it. It is written for the finished setup: the website lives in the Big Sky GitHub organisation, and everything on the Google side lives on the facilities Google account.

The big picture

Phones and computers. Staff open the website. Every tick and note is saved on the device as it is entered.
↓ ↑
The website (GitHub). A handful of HTML files published with GitHub Pages. No server, no database, no logins.
↓ ↑
The Apps Script web app (facilities Google account). Receives the app’s requests: “give me the list”, “update this space”.
↓ ↑
The Maintenance List sheet (facilities Google account). The one shared copy of the data.

Each piece has one job, and none of them needs a paid service or a developer to keep running.

Why it is built this way

  • Works on a phone, in a plant room. Everything is saved on the device first, and sent when there is signal.
  • Nothing to maintain. There is no server to patch. If GitHub and Google are up, the app is up.
  • One place for shared data. Only the Maintenance List and check dates are shared. Ticks and notes stay on the phone until PDFs are generated.

How a month flows through the system

  1. A person ticks Pass or Fail on their phone. It is saved on that phone only.
  2. They tap Generate PDFs. The app builds the PDFs on the phone, and sends one request per space to the script.
  3. The script makes the Maintenance List match the checklist: new fails are added, open ones are updated, fixed-on-the-spot ones are resolved. It also records the date each section was checked.
  4. Every phone refreshes the list every minute, so everyone sees the same thing. The “3/4 this month” progress is worked out from the recorded check dates.
  5. At month end, the app builds the summary email from the list. A person sends it with the PDFs attached.

What is stored where

WhereWhat
On each device (browser storage)Ticks, notes and readings; the person’s name; checkpoint edits not yet made permanent; a record of what has already been sent to the list; a retry queue for anything that could not be sent. Clearing website data on the browser erases these.
The Google SheetEvery issue on the Maintenance List, and the date each section of each space was last checked.
GitHubThe app itself and the default list of checkpoints.
Drive (or Files)The PDFs, wherever the person saves them from the share sheet.
The website and its filesGitHub, what each file is, updating

Where it lives

The site is one repository in the Big Sky GitHub organisation, published with GitHub Pages from the main branch, root folder. The repository’s Settings page, under Pages, shows the live address. Keep the list of people with write access short: anyone who can commit can change what the whole team sees.

The files

/                          repository root
  index.html               the main app
  instructions.html        the team guide (this page)
  satellite/
    omega.html             Omega Place page
    14a.html               14A page
    hoxton.html            Hoxton page
    omega-guide.html       short guide for the Omega Place manager
    14a-guide.html         short guide for the 14A manager
    hoxton-guide.html      short guide for the Hoxton manager
FileWhat it is
index.htmlThe full app for the facilities team: every building and space, the Maintenance List, the monthly email, the Satellites tab.
instructions.htmlThis guide. Opened from the app’s Help.
satellite/omega.htmlThe same app, set to one site only, for the Omega Place manager. Its guide is omega-guide.html.
satellite/14a.htmlThe same, for 14A. Guide: 14a-guide.html.
satellite/hoxton.htmlThe same, for Hoxton. Guide: hoxton-guide.html.

How each file is built

  • Every file is self-contained. The code, styling, logo and PDF library are all inside the one file. There is no build step and nothing else to host.
  • The pages link by relative address (./satellite/omega.html). The folder layout above must be kept for the links to work.
  • Satellite pages are the same app with a switch turned on, so a site manager only sees their own site. Each one keeps its own storage on the device, so two pages never overwrite each other.

Settings near the top of the code

NameWhat it does
APP_VERSIONThe number shown at the top right. Bump it on every release so people can tell which version they have.
MAINTENANCE_API_URLThe address of the Apps Script web app (the /exec link).
MAINTENANCE_SHEET_URLThe Google Sheet address, used by the Open Sheet button.
FACILITIES_EMAILWhere the monthly email is addressed.
CHECKPOINTS_DEFAULTThe built-in list of every checkpoint in every space. Edits made in the app are saved on the phone and replace it for that phone only, until they are built in here.
SATELLITE_SITESThe list of satellite sites shown on the main app’s Satellites tab, with the section types each one uses.
EMAIL_INCLUDES_SATELLITESWhether satellite sites appear in the main monthly email. Off, because each manager sends their own.

Publishing an update

  1. On GitHub, open the repository, choose Add file, then Upload files, and drag in the changed files, keeping the satellite folder where it is.
  2. Commit. GitHub Pages republishes in a minute or two.
  3. Open the app and check the version number at the top right. If it is old, close the tab and reopen it.
Rolling back. Every commit is kept. If an update causes a problem, open the file’s history on GitHub and restore the previous version.
The Google Sheet and scriptOn the facilities Google account

Who owns it

The Google Sheet and the script both belong to the facilities Google account, not to a person. That way they keep working when staff change. The account’s Drive is also the natural place to save the PDFs.

The Google Sheet

Named Big Sky Compliance, Maintenance List. It has two tabs, and the script finds them by name:

TabColumns (row 1, exactly)
MaintenanceID, Status, Date Flagged, Space, Compliance Type, Checkpoint, Checkpoint ID, Issue, Action Note, Resolved At
CheckLogSpace, Compliance Type, Last Checked, Checked By
  • Maintenance has one row per issue. Open issues have Status “Open”; resolved ones keep their row, with the time resolved.
  • CheckLog has one row per space and section, holding the last date it went through a PDF run. This is what “Last checked” and “3/4 this month” are worked out from.
Do not rename the tabs, rename the headings, or delete the heading row. The script reads by those names. Reading, filtering and adding extra columns to the right are all safe.

The Apps Script

The script lives inside the sheet (Extensions, Apps Script), and the source is the file MaintenanceListScript.gs. It is published as a web app:

Execute asThe facilities Google account
Who has accessAnyone with the link
AddressThe /exec link, built into every page as MAINTENANCE_API_URL

What it can do:

RequestUsed for
ReadSends the list and the check dates to the app. Happens when the app opens and every minute.
syncSpaceThe main one. Sent when PDFs are generated: makes the list match the checklist, and records the check dates.
updateNoteSaves an Action note typed on the Maintenance List.
resolveMarks an issue resolved.
add, logCheckOlder single-item requests, kept as a fallback.
The web address is inside the page code, and anyone who has it can read and write the list. Share the app’s own links with people, not the script address.

Updating the script

  1. Open the sheet on the facilities account, then Extensions, Apps Script.
  2. Replace the whole script with the new MaintenanceListScript.gs and save.
  3. Deploy, Manage deployments, choose the pencil on the existing deployment, set Version to New version, and Deploy. Editing the existing deployment keeps the same address.
Choosing New deployment instead creates a different address, and every page would then need the new address built in.
Common admin jobsUpdate, add a site, handover, move accounts

Update the app

See The website and its files, “Publishing an update”.

Make checkpoint changes permanent

  1. Make the changes on one phone using Edit checkpoints.
  2. Tap Export All and copy what it gives you.
  3. Replace the CHECKPOINTS_DEFAULT block in index.html with it, bump APP_VERSION, and publish. A satellite site’s checkpoints are replaced in that site’s own page.

Add a new satellite site

  1. Copy an existing page in satellite/ (for example 14a.html) and rename it for the new site.
  2. Change the site name, its short key and the section types it uses, and set its checkpoints.
  3. Add the site to SATELLITE_SITES in index.html so it appears on the Satellites tab.
  4. Copy a guide from satellite/ too, and change the site name, so the manager gets their own short guide.

Hand a satellite page to its manager

The satellite pages show a small Back to main app link at the top, which is there for testing. Remove it before handover, so the manager only sees their own site. Then send them the page’s link and their guide.

Move to a different Google account

  1. Create a new sheet with the two tabs and headings described in The Google Sheet and script.
  2. Paste in the script, and deploy it as a web app as above.
  3. Replace MAINTENANCE_API_URL and MAINTENANCE_SHEET_URL in every page (the main app and all satellite pages), then publish.
  4. Copy the old sheet’s rows across if the history is needed.
Where things are storedYour phone, the sheet and the PDFs
WhatWhere it lives
Your ticks, notes and readingsOn your phone, in the browser. Not shared. Clearing the browser’s website data erases them, so generate the PDFs before doing that.
Checkpoint editsOn your phone until you Export All and send them on.
The Maintenance List and check datesIn a shared Google Sheet. The same for everyone.
The PDFsWherever you save them from the share sheet (Drive, Files).
The app itselfOn GitHub Pages. The version number is at the top right of the screen.
Words used in the app
CheckpointOne thing that is checked: a light, an extinguisher, a door, a tap.
SectionOne of the four compliance types in a space.
FlaggedMarked Fail on the checklist.
OutstandingFlagged and not fixed on the spot, or open on the Maintenance List.
Action taken / Action noteWhat is being done. Written on the checklist as Action taken; shown on the Maintenance List as Action note. They stay in step.
Fixed on the spotSorted at the time. On the PDF, not on the list.
ResolvedAn issue on the Maintenance List that has been properly fixed and closed.
SatelliteA site outside the main building with its own page and manager.
